newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close weaker on triple-witching.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close weaker on triple-witching.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended Wednesday weaker than New York after outperforming it for most of the session, as volatility took hold ahead of Friday's quarterly triple-witching.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 40.32 points to reach 6088.96, only a few points off its intra-day low. Trading was light at 91.3 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.16 billion).
Wall Street closed 18.88 points weaker at 6877.68, about 50 points above its intra-day low.
"New York recovered a lot more than Canada did," said portfolio manager Josef Schachter of Schachter Asset Management.

Markets were volatile ahead of the quarterly triple witching -- the expiration of options, futures and options on futures. "It was kind of a funny market," Schachter said. "You've got a little nervousness over Friday's triple-witching."

Also overhanging North American markets were concerns that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike short-term interest rates to quash inflation, analysts said. As rates rise, bond yields increase and bond prices drop, luring investors who sell interest-sensitive issues such as banks. The U.S. Federal Reserve is expected to increase rates at a March 25 meeting.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-groups, all except for oils lost ground. Falling sectors included conglomerates, media, consumer products and base metals.
Declining issues beat out advances 608 to 382 while another 290 traded unchanged.
In individual stocks, Wascana Energy Inc. shares extended their rally, rising 0.10 to 20.55 on more than 6.1 million shares.
On Tuesday Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. made a white knight C$2 billion ($1.45 billion) bid for Wascana. CanOxy rose 1.10 to 26.25 on more than 5.7 million shares.

Closely watched prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd. lost 0.40 to 17.25 after news that Mike de Guzman, chief geologist at its Busang gold discovery in Indonesia, fell (243.8 meters) 800 feet from a helicopter.
